name: Jeiel
overview: Jeiel was a male member of the tribe of Levi, specifically a descendant of Elizaphan, as noted in 2 Chronicles 29:13. He belonged to the Kohathite family line, which descended from Uzziel, son of Kohath, who was a son of Levi. This lineage situates Jeiel within the Levitical priestly heritage important for temple service.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeiel means 'G-d has preserved,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning consistent with Hebrew naming practices. This proper name is explicitly recorded in 2 Chronicles 29:13 and was not given directly by God but carries a significant meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Jeiel is explicitly identified as a descendant of Elizaphan (also spelled Elzaphan), linking him to a known Levitical family. Beyond this, Scripture does not record additional family relationships for Jeiel beyond what is noted in his unique attribute.
scriptureSignificance: Jeiel's significance lies in his position within the Levitical Kohathite lineage, which was entrusted with particular duties in the service of the tabernacle and temple. Being a descendant of Elizaphan connects him to a notable branch of the Levites, emphasizing the continuity of Levitical service and faithfulness to God's covenant community. His mention in 2 Chronicles 29:13 situates him within the historical restoration efforts during King Hezekiah's reign.
